why: All three checks confirm the finding; I could not refute it. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: third-party-integrations.md:327 carries the sentence character-for-character, under '## Best practices for organizations' -> '### Invest in documentation and memory'. The whole line was read; it is a single-clause bullet with no reversing second half, and the sibling bullet ('Repository-level') plus the trailing 'Learn more in Memory and CLAUDE.md files' confirm this is a real tier list, not prose. Corroborated on a second page: memory.md:58 gives the tier its own row in the precedence table -- '| **Managed policy** | macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md; Linux and WSL /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md; Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md | Organization-wide instructions managed by IT/DevOps | ... | All users in organization |' -- and repeats the three paths at :279-281. So it is a specified, highest-precedence memory tier, not a deployment suggestion. (2) CITED FILE: packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:32 CONTEXT_FILE_PATTERNS = ['agents.md','claude.md','claude.local.md']; :37-41 CONTEXT_FILE_SCOPE_BY_PATTERN maps them to ent/project/local; :42-47 CONTEXT_FILE_SCOPE_ORDER = ent 0, project 1, user 2, local 3; :36 USER_GLOBAL_CONTEXT_FILE_PATTERN = 'claude.md', read from getUserGlobalContextDirectory() = join(homeDir, '.nessy-agent') (:136-138). Reads exactly as claimed. (3) ONE LAYER UP -- and this is where the finding could have died, but does not. The cited path is the LEGACY route: packages/shared/AGENTS.md records that buildVolatileContextParts skips the project-context-file block whenever the capability runtime is active, 'which is every normal send', and that instruction/memory layers ride BaseAgent.buildPinnedCapabilityContext() instead. I therefore re-checked the LIVE route. capabilities/native-sources.ts:buildNativeCapabilityInventory has exactly three roots -- global (CONFIG_DIR = ~/.nessy-agent: skills, agents, mcp.json, hooks.json, MEMORY.md, rules/), workspace (context.workspaceRootPath), and project (trusted cwd, .nessy-agent/ + portable .claude/.agents tiers, PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = ['AGENTS.md','CLAUDE.md','CLAUDE.local.md'] at :82). capabilities/resolver.ts:863-869 scopeSpecificity enumerates the entire scope vocabulary: project 3, workspace 2, global 1, builtin 0. There is no system/enterprise scope on either path, so the consequence survives on the live path as well as the legacy one. ONE LAYER DOWN: could an admin ship standards some other way? No. Managed policy is 34 keys (managed-policy.ts:501-533 MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS) and not one carries instruction, memory, systemPrompt or context content -- grep for those terms in managed-policy.ts returns zero. Force-enabling a plugin does not substitute either: 'instruction' and 'memory' are NATIVE_BINDING_KINDS only (resolver.ts:897-900); grep for 'instruction'/'memory' across packages/shared/src/plugins/ and format-adapters/ returns zero, so a plugin cannot contribute either kind. SIBLING SUBSYSTEM: the finding names the right one. The system-directory tier genuinely does exist in this fork, and only for policy -- managed-policy-loader.ts:44-52 returns '/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json' (darwin), '/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json' (linux), %ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json (win32), pinned by managed-policy-loader.test.ts:99-101, plus a managed-policy.d/ drop-in dir at :62-67. A NUL-safe grep -a for Nessy/CLAUDE, nessy/CLAUDE, Nessy/AGENTS, Nessy/MEMORY across packages/ and apps/ returns 0 hits: those three system directories are read for one JSON policy file and nothing else. OWNER DECISION? No. The nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. None concerns a context-file or memory tier. DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE? No. The page-level note in the sweep marks third-party-integrations 'inapplicable' as a deployment comparison (Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/Console topologies this fork does not ship) and the coverage map row 154 says 'vne produkta' -- but that same note explicitly carves this item OUT: 'Two items were checked against our code anyway: the fable model tier is already known to our model metadata, and the organization-wide memory tier is not.' An org-wide memory tier is not a subscription flow, not a cloud-provider topology, and not a rename; the fork already implements the Nessy-renamed equivalent of Claude's system directory for policy, so the tier is architecturally in scope and simply absent for memory. Residual imprecision in the finding, not enough to refute: the evidence cites the legacy prompts/system.ts path rather than the live capability path, and 'one read-only user-global claude.md in the config directory' understates the live global tier, which also reads ~/.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md and ~/.nessy-agent/rules/, plus a whole workspace tier. Neither changes the conclusion.
correctedState: There is no system-directory (organization-wide) tier for context or memory files on either the legacy or the live path. Legacy route: packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:32-47 reads agents.md/claude.md/claude.local.md from the working directory (scopes ent/project/local) plus one read-only user-global claude.md from getUserGlobalContextDirectory() = ~/.nessy-agent (:36, :136-138). Live route (the one every normal send uses, per packages/shared/AGENTS.md): capabilities/native-sources.ts:buildNativeCapabilityInventory reads instruction and memory files from exactly three roots -- global ~/.nessy-agent (MEMORY.md, rules/), workspace root (PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md at :82, .agents/rules, .claude/rules), and trusted project (.nessy-agent/ plus portable .claude/.agents tiers) -- and capabilities/resolver.ts:863-869 enumerates the complete scope vocabulary as project/workspace/global/builtin. The system directory IS wired in this fork, but for policy only: managed-policy-loader.ts:44-52 resolves /Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json, /etc/nessy/managed-policy.json and %ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json (plus a managed-policy.d/ drop-in dir at :62-67), and none of the 34 keys in MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (managed-policy.ts:501-533) carries instruction, memory or system-prompt content. Plugins cannot close the gap either: 'instruction' and 'memory' are native-only binding kinds (resolver.ts:897-900), absent from every plugin adapter, so a managed enabledPlugins force-enable cannot deliver company-wide standards. Claude's tier is specified in two places -- third-party-integrations.md:327 and memory.md:58/:279-281, where it is the highest-precedence 'Managed policy' memory row. Closing the gap means adding one read of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md from the same system directory the policy loader already resolves, bound above the project tier.
